newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt welcomes U.S. stand on Jewish settlements.
newsitem.headline: Egypt welcomes U.S. stand on Jewish settlements.

text.p: Egypt welcomed U.S. criticism of Israeli settlement activity in the West Bank on Thursday but said it was pessimistic about Middle East peace talks.
Foreign Minister Amr Moussa also dismissed as "nonsense" Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's talk of Arabs waging psychological war on Israel.
Moussa said he had recently discussed the peace process with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher. "What I can confirm is that I am not optimistic so far," he told reporters.
The minister was speaking to reporters after briefing Mubarak on his visit to France, which ended on Wednesday.

On Washington's more forthright criticism of Jewish settlements, seen by Palestinians as a major obstacle to any agreement, Moussa said: "We welcome this position. Their position is good and clearly shows the position of the United States as a sponsor of the peace process."
Asked what he thought of Netanyahu's "psychological war" remark, the minister said: "That is nonsense."

Speaking to Israeli army radio on Tuesday, the Israeli prime minister said: "The Arabs are waging a psychological war against us, are trying to create a sort of comprehensive Arab front and threaten us with wars and intifadas (uprisings)...with the goal of weakening our position and our just demands."
